One EventValidation gotcha encountered and resolved: a 'rblRepeatClient' RadioButtonList (repeat-client question) is rendered on the very first GET but is NOT re-rendered in the response to the state-selection postback -- submitting any value for it on the final POST throws a hard HTTP 500 ('Invalid postback or callback argument', traced to RadioButtonList.LoadPostData), the same 'field for a control not in the current DOM breaks the postback' failure mode already documented for Old Republic's ReoList and Knight Barry's OR county gotchas. Fix: omit rblRepeatClient entirely from the final POST (it is not required once absent from the rendered form). methodology: Harvested via Stewart's discoverable `/api/SRC/*` JSON REST API (stewartratecalculator.com), driven entirely by plain HTTP GET/POST (Python requests.Session(), cookie jar) with no browser/JS execution and no personal-data fields, replaying the full recipe documented in this project's CALCULATORS.md (2026-08-14 'SOLVED' entry): GET the LoanEstimate/Netsheet page to scrape a fresh antiforgery cookie + __RequestVerificationToken; GET /api/SRC/propertysearch to resolve the county FIPS code and a default zip; GET /api/SRC/providers to find the county's real settlement office(s) (used to set ProviderID on the QuoteType=3 flow so the itemized settlement-fee list is populated -- an empty ProviderID silently returns a null itemized list); GET /api/SRC/statesettings and /api/SRC/ernstlookup for state-level defaults; build the QuoteRequestRoot JSON by hand (Owner's Policy $500,000 / Lender's Policy $400,000, BASIC coverage, standard Sale/Purchase with Mortgage transaction); POST /api/SRC/quote twice -- QuoteType=2 (Netsheet, pageBuyerSeller=seller) for Recording/CFPB2015 transfer-tax figures, and QuoteType=3 (LoanEstimate, pageBuyerSeller=buyer, IsCalculatePremium=True, IsCalculateTitleServiceFee=True) for the itemized Pricing.TitleServiceFee.ItemizedTitleServiceFeeList settlement-fee line items. One new gotcha found and fixed this session: stewartratecalculator.com's bare apex domain 301-redirects every POST to the www subdomain, and that redirect's response body hangs indefinitely on this sandbox's proxied connection (a 30s+ read timeout with 0 bytes received) -- fixed by targeting https://www.stewartratecalculator.com directly, skipping the apex redirect entirely; this is an environment/proxy artifact, not a sign the endpoint is blocked. Also confirmed the documented /api/SRC/providers gotcha firsthand: for a single-provider county the response's `Provider` field is a bare object, not a one-element list -- must be normalized before indexing or ProviderID silently stays empty and every itemized-fee list comes back null (looks exactly like a genuine empty result).
